profile.name: Raf
profile.intro: Full-stack developer working across the stack — from database schema and APIs to the last pixel of the UI. I like boring infrastructure, clear code, and products that just work.
profile.photoAlt: Portrait of Rafael Vincent D. Medina

paragraphs: I'm a software developer who enjoys turning messy requirements into simple, well-structured systems. Most of my work lives on the web: React and Next.js on the front, Node, Python and Postgres behind it.
I care about the things that keep a codebase healthy over time — sensible abstractions, good tests, readable pull requests, and shipping in small, safe steps.

projects.title: DTR for Internship
projects.description: DTR System is a web-based Daily Time Record application built for interns to track their daily attendance and rendered hours. Users can register, log in, and record their AM/PM time-in and time-out, including half-day entries. The system automatically computes hours worked and undertime, shows a dashboard with weekly and total hours, and keeps a monthly attendance history with remarks. Users can download their monthly DTR as a printable PDF and reset forgotten passwords by email.

projects.title: Lord of the Rims
projects.description:
Lord of the Rims is a full-stack car rental web app built as my PHP final project.

Customers can browse and filter a fleet of luxury vehicles, sign up for an account, and book a car using an interactive calendar that greys out dates already taken. Each booking calculates its total price automatically, and customers can track or cancel their reservations from a "My Bookings" page.

Admins get a dedicated dashboard with live stats (fleet size, bookings, revenue and customers), can add or edit vehicles with photo uploads, and move bookings through each stage from pending to confirmed, active and completed.

projects.title: Thesis Archiving
projects.description: Thesis Archive System is a generic web-based repository built as our college thesis project. It replaces manual record-keeping of research papers with a searchable online archive for both the College and Senior High School departments.Students can log in to submit their thesis with its abstract, authors, advisors and PDF file, then track whether it is pending, approved or rejected. Administrators and student assistants review submissions and manage the collection: theses, academic programs, user accounts and the site's branding. Visitors can browse by department, filter by program and year, search by title, author or abstract, and read the PDFs directly in the browser.
